scoring_justification: Full recompute of the elastodynamic simulation is infeasible in the verifier. The modal amplitudes are compared to the paper's reported values with generous tolerance; derived metrics are checked against structural thresholds.

hidden_assets.generation_method: copied directly from the paper's numerical example for the PZT‑5/steel case at 78 kHz
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the exact values reported in the paper; they represent the target of reproduction and are not fabricated.

hidden_assets.source_provenance: paper's qualitative claims and Fig. 2‑6 (peak frequency ≈78 kHz, stress ratio >>1, shear dominance, attenuation depth within mm range)
hidden_assets.generation_method: extracted from the paper's stated peak frequency and structural claims; thresholds ensure a correct reproduction meets the paper's findings.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These thresholds reflect the paper's findings; a correct reproduction must satisfy them.

outputs.description: Modal amplitude constants A_n (normal loading) and B_n (shear loading) for the first four odd modes at 78 kHz.
Verification metrics: stress ratio in contact area, shear dominance flag, frequency of peak surface displacement, and 1/e attenuation depth.

output_contract.notes: The agent must implement the entire analytical/numerical pipeline: Fourier expansion, half-space elastodynamic solutions via Fourier integrals and contour integration, assembly and solution of the 2N×2N linear system, and post-processing of fields. All material properties (steel, PZT-5) are publicly available from standard references. The scored modal amplitudes will be checked against the paper's reported values with order-of-magnitude tolerance; the verification metrics must satisfy the stated structural thresholds.

steps.description: Compare A and B arrays to paper gold with relative tolerance 2.0 (i.e., up to 200% error allowed). Sign must match.
Check that stress_ratio >= threshold, shear_dominant is True, peak_frequency within [73,83] kHz, attenuation_depth in (0,10) mm.
